correctness.rationale: All parities and boundary degree values are covered. Conditioning on available edges proves a finite exact recursion; a uniform ordinary-pair removal permutation yields an exact survival product. Its hypergeometric hazard has expectation \(\alpha H_{(N-2)/2}\), variance \(O(\alpha)\), and integrated log-correction expectation \(O(\alpha+\alpha^2)\), proving both finite and infinite limiting hazard regimes analytically. A standalone exact verifier cross-checks 40 finite order-degree pairs by two independent formulations.

value.rationale: A dense-core one-defect graph is a natural test of jamming versus perfect-matching feasibility. It has perfect matchings at every positive exceptional degree, yet exhibits a sharp \(N/\log N\) boundary and universal \(e^{-c}\) limiting failure probability, resolving a nontrivial asymptotic regime rather than an arbitrary small-graph count. The finite recurrence provides further reproducible information.
